ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against PEP lists (as defined by GAFI/FINMA), UN Security Council sanctions as implemented by SECO (State Secretariat of Economic Affairs), Swiss domestic sanctions under the Economic Sanctions Ordinance, OFAC SDN list for USD transactions, and the EU consolidated sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates, including source of funds verification and independent verification of beneficial ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Central Business Name Index – Zefix (www.zefix.ch) in conjunction with the local cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in the Romansh script? (Latin script), and may be in German, French, Italian, or Romansh. The name must not be misleading, must clearly indicate the purpose of the company, and must include the legal form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG'. When a foreign-language name is used, it must comply with the same distinctiveness and truthfulness standards. The registry will refuse names that are identical or confusingly similar to an existing trademark or registered company name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any term implying public-law status or membership in a regulated profession without prior ministerial approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the Commercial Register Office, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the cantonal supervisory authority (Department of Justice or Trade, as applicable) within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must state the grounds and request re-examination. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may further appeal to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) within 30 days. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a new name reservation application with a proposed corrective name without prejudice to the original business plan.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is not accepted as a registered office for an Aktiengesellschaft; a physical operational office or at minimum a permanent physical registered office must exist within Switzerland, being a place where legal documents, citations, and notices can be officially served. For an esports community platform, a managed physical office with administrative presence is compliant, but pure virtual mailbox arrangements are prohibited.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% probability during the first year of operation; 10% in subsequent years if the registered office is a genuine office provided by a licensed corporate services provider. Unannounced inspections are more likely if the company engages nominee directors or if there are discrepancies in the commercial register filings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 620 to 763 (Aktiengesellschaft), in particular Article 626 (nominal capital), Article 629 (minimum paid-up capital), and Article 641 (registration application).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) of the canton of the registered office, e.g. Canton of Zug, under the supervisory authority of the Federal Department of Justice and Police.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Commercial Register Entry (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister) together with the notarised deed of incorporation, Articles of Association (Statuten), and minutes of the constitutive shareholders' meeting.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal capital of CHF 100,000; at least CHF 20,000 (20%) must be paid up before registration. The paid-up amount may be held in a blocked bank escrow account until the Commercial Register entry is made, and the bank confirmation must be filed with the application.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WE, the duly appointed subscribers, resolve as follows: FIRST: the share capital of CHF 100,000 is subscribed in full; each subscriber accepts the number of registered shares set opposite his/her name and undertakes to pay the required 20% minimum contribution into an escrow account in favour of the company. SECOND: the registered office of the company is fixed at [Zug/Zurich], Switzerland; the address of the company as designated by the board is adopted as the legal domicile. THIRD: [Name] is elected Chairman, [Name] is appointed CEO, and [Name] is appointed Secretary; each officer accepts office. FOURTH: the officers are authorised to complete all registrations, licences and banking formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and notarise Articles of Association and founding deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss public notary (öffentliche Urkundsperson) in the canton of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association including company name, domicile, purpose (esports tournament platform, software publishing, community management), share capital, share types, and board organisation. The notary must certify the deed and attest the signatures of all founding shareholders and board members.
required_dossiers: Declaration of compliance with Arts. OR 626 and OR 629
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notary queries inconsistencies in the deed, submit an amended deed by means of a supplementary notarial protocol; no new shareholder approval is needed for purely formal corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open blocked escrow account and obtain bank confirmation of paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank (or Swiss licensed securities dealer providing escrow/blocked account services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the company being formed. Deposit at least CHF 20,000 paid-in capital. Obtain a bank confirmation (Bankbestätigung) stating the amount held to the free disposal of the company upon registration and that no right of disposal exists in the interim.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association and notarised deed
Proof of identification for beneficial owners (AML/KYC forms)
Bank account opening forms and signature cards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the beneficial-owner documentation, supply a valid source-of-wealth statement or revised KYC package; escrow release can be re-confirmed by the bank after cure and resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File commercial register application with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office, e.g. Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarised deed, board resolution approving the filing, bank escrow confirmation, and identification forms for all signatories through the SwissElex/eGRIS digital interface or in person. Pay the registration fee. The commercial register will verify the name, capital, purpose, and legal form before issuing the certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Bank confirmation of minimum paid-up capital
Identification and specimen signatures of board members
Consent notifications for name and purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency letter, the gap must be cured within the deadline, usually 10 to 20 days, by submitting supplementary notarised documents, revised statutes, or corrected KYC information; in case of unlawful refusal, an appeal can be lodged with the Administrative Court of the canton.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with federal social security and tax authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), cantonal tax administration, and compensation fund (Ausgleichskasse)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, request the Company Identification Number (UID) automatically assigned by the Federal Statistical Office. Register as an employer with the compensation fund for AHV/IV/EO, with Suva for occupational accident insurance, and with the cantonal tax administration for corporate income tax and VAT purposes. File a VAT registration if annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000.
required_dossiers: List of employees and payroll data (for social insurance)
Application for employer registration (AHV) and accident insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social security files are rejected, obtain duplicate Commercial Register extracts and proof of authorised signatory; corrections must be filed electronically without fees if submitted within the statutory cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain general municipal business permit and notify building authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Business Licensing Office (Bewilligungsbehörde der Gemeinde) in the registered office municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a general business registration/operating permit for the corporate office premises. If any physical server room is installed, submit a building and use notification to the community building authority and an electrical safety declaration if uninterruptible power supply units or high-density server racks exceed local thresholds.
required_dossiers: Site plan and floor plan of the office/technical rooms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses an occupancy permit, provide a structural load certificate or reduce server load density; appeal the negative ruling to the cantonal department of economic development within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial sector licensing authority applies to esports tournament platforms under ISIC 5820; the general business licence authority of the municipality, together with the cantonal environmental authority, supervises any physical infrastructure.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; if physical server hosting is introduced, the additional title could be a 'Bewilligung für gewerbliche Tätigkeit' (general business and building occupancy permit).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) with the cantonal environmental protection agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal EIA for pure digital services; optional registration may be required for emission sources such as backup generators or cooling systems if a physical server room is installed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater discharge for digital platform activity. If physical equipment is installed, comply with the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) for backup generator exhaust and the Ordinance on Movement of Waste (VVEA) for electronic waste; VOC emissions from offices are limited to maintenance standards under the Ordinance on Chemical Risk Reduction (ChemRRV).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance (Feuerpolizei) for office and technical rooms; structural load inspection for server racks exceeding 5 kN/m² floor loading; occupational health and safety checks under the Labour Act and ArGV 3, including workplace lighting, ergonomic workstation assessment, and accident insurance coverage through Suva or another approved insurer.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC/FTA) in Berne; cantonal tax administrations; corporate and VAT registrations are handled via the Federal Tax Administration's ePortal (www.eportal.ch) and the Swiss Central Business Name Index (Zefix) for UID issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG), the statutory identification is the Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer (UID), issued by the Swiss Federal Statistical Office after entry into the Commercial Register (canton) and published on Zefix. The UID automatically serves as the VAT identifier for Swiss VAT purposes (MWSTID/TVA). For foreign entities without a Swiss registered office, registration for Swiss VAT is required when carrying out taxable supplies in Switzerland and can be performed electronically through the FTA ePortal. Tax registration steps: (1) incorporate the AG with local commercial registrar; (2) obtain UID from Zefix; (3) if taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed CHF 100,000, electronically submit Form 0810 (VAT registration questionnaire) to the Federal Tax Administration through ePortal; (4) designate a Swiss VAT-collecting agent (representative) if no branch or residence in Switzerland; (5) await validation and issuance of MWSTID, and register for use of the e-billing/online portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss federal and cantonal tax law does not provide a check-the-box election. The AG is always taxed at entity level (corporate income tax on profit and cantonal/communal taxes on profit and equity after the federal and cantonal tax harmonization). Equity tax (capital tax) is assessed at cantonal level and is not avoidable by entity classification election. A Swiss group might elect for 'Status of the fiscal year' (fiscal period) or group taxation ('Steuerliche Dekonsolidierung/Organschaft') only for certain cantonal and federal purposes, notably carrying forward losses and allocating consolidated profit; no hybrid mismatch check-the-box elections are possible. For foreign hybrid instruments or entities, Switzerland applies transparent treatment under Swiss law; entity-level elections are not available. The AG must file its statutory and tax accounts in CHF, using Swiss GAAP or IFRS for accounting purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Turnover threshold for VAT registration: CHF 100,000 per year (Art. 10 para 2 (a) LTVA, since 1 January 2019) where taxable supplies are made in Switzerland or from abroad into Switzerland; foreign supplies of electronic services are generally covered by a separate rule (Art. 107 para 1 LTVA) requiring VAT registration without the CHF 100,000 de minimis when supplied to Swiss private individuals, unless the supplier uses the 'simplified registration' procedure for electronically supplied services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping regime. E-invoicing is voluntary. The mandatory electronic e-invoice standard (eBill and the QR-bill invoice standard) applies to B2G transactions as of 2023, but there is no central tax-authority clearance of every invoice. For VAT purposes, all invoices must satisfy the statutory content requirements of Art. 26 LTVA, including the MWSTID/TVA identification, date, supplier and recipient names, nature and quantity of supply, consideration, and tax amount. The Federal Tax Administration offers an online 'VAT invoice generator' but does not require prior approval. For export documentation, e-dec (electronic customs declaration) and statcards are used.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: In Switzerland, supplies of goods and services to foreign destinations can be zero-rated (0% VAT) if the goods are physically exported and the supplier retains documentary proof, or if the services are supplied to a foreign business or foreign recipient at a place of supply outside Switzerland and meet the conditions of Art. 23 para 4 LTVA and the OLTVA (VAT Ordinance). For an esports community platform, zero-rating is commonly available for: (1) electronically supplied tournament services, matchmaking subscriptions, virtual goods, and advertising services to foreign players/partners where the recipient is a foreign business (B2B) or the private recipient is established in a foreign country; (2) export of physical esports merchandise; (3) ancillary services (e.g., tournament organization) directly related to exported goods. Required proof: the supplier must be able to demonstrate the ultimate recipient's business location abroad via a Swiss or EU VAT identification number, contracts, and invoice, and demonstrate actual use of the service abroad. Where the platform provides services to Swiss residents, Swiss VAT at the standard rate (currently 8.1%) applies unless a lower rate is indicated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Export Customs Declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung/e-dec) with electronic filing reference (e-dec number)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR (transport document) confirming physical export of goods
Commercial invoice issued to the foreign customer (B2B) with full description and VAT ID
Import certificate from destination country when required (e.g., for precious metals, pharmaceuticals)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration may conduct targeted audits of zero-rated supplies for up to five years (ordinary limitation), and up to ten years post-assessment where intentional tax evasion is discovered. Penalties for false zero-rating or claim of VAT refund without proper export substantiation: (a) tax payable is reinstated with default interest at up to 5% per annum; (b) a penalty of up to three times the evaded tax for intentional tax evasion (Art. 174 para 1 LTVA); (c) negligence fines up to twice the evaded tax (Art. 175 LTVA); (d) administrative fines up to CHF 10,000 per violation for formal non-compliance; (e) criminal prosecution for tax fraud, counterfeiting, or false documentation. The FTA also denies refund claims and imposes clawback of previously refunded amounts. Internal compliance guidance requires permanent retention of all export and remittance documentation for at least ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank, Banque nationale suisse, Banca nazionale svizzera)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible on both capital and current account. Switzerland maintains no foreign exchange controls, no mandatory central bank approval for current payments, no prior licensing for profit remittance, and no prohibition on holding, converting, or transferring foreign currency. A Swiss AG may freely receive revenue from esports matchmaking, tournament fees, subscription services, and prize-pool settlements in EUR, USD, or other currencies, and may remit dividends, loan repayments, service fees, and royalties abroad. The only meaningful friction is Swiss anticipatory tax of 35% on dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders, which is generally refundable in full or in part under an applicable double taxation agreement; this is a withholding tax matter and not an FX convertibility or capital-control restriction. Switzerland does not in practice require any balance-of-payments licensing even for large cross-border transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law and the Swiss National Bank impose no statutory timeline for repatriation of export or service proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio to CHF, and no surrender requirement. Proceeds related to the esports platform, whether received as SWIFT credits, card settlements, or via third-party payment gateways such as Stripe and PayPal, remain freely disposable in the treasury account. The SNB retains only statistical balance-of-payments reporting powers, which do not require conversion, escrow, or repatriation of funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / API-Accessible Clearing and Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse AG (member of UBS Group AG)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as an ancillary receivables-collection rail, but Low as the sole treasury banking channel. Non-Swiss EMIs and neobanks cannot participate in Swiss SIC/euroSIC clearing and cannot issue domestic CHF IBANs; they must settle indirectly through Swiss or EU correspondent banks. Regulatory constraint: a Swiss AG that accumulates player funds or merchant settlement proceeds on a foreign EMI may be treated as accepting deposits from the public without FINMA authorization, contrary to Article 1 of the Swiss Banking Act, and may also create insolvency-exposure risk outside the Swiss deposit-protection framework. EU or UK EMI licenses are not passportable into Switzerland. The legally robust route is to operate a Swiss tier-1 operational account as the treasury anchor while using Stripe and PayPal solely as acquiring rails settling into that Swiss account; the platform should not rely on any offshore EMI for liquidity custody or for serving as the account of record.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss law and FINMA supervisory practice do not impose a blanket statutory requirement that directors appear physically in a branch. However, account opening remains a discretionary, risk-based process for each bank. For a Swiss AG with non-resident directors or beneficial owners, tier-1 banks and cantonal banks typically require (i) an interactive video-identification interview of at least one board member or economic beneficiary with the bank's compliance officer under the AMLA/FinSA identification framework, and (ii) in practice, either one physical visit to Switzerland or notarized and apostilled identity verification performed by a Swiss embassy, Swiss notary, or certified Swiss attorney before the account is activated. Purely remote onboarding with no physical touchpoint and no reputable Swiss legal adviser is generally rejected, particularly where the funding source includes crypto assets or non-EEA UBOs. The onboarding dossier must include a signed board resolution authorizing the account opening and specifying the transaction profile of the esports platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner with opaque multi-tier structure resident in a non-EEA or FATF-monitored jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss Commercial Register excerpt, notarized and apostilled passport and identity documents, full ownership-chain chart, statutory declaration of beneficial ownership under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act, 12 months of bank statements and tax returns for each UBO, negative sanctions/media/PEP screening report from a regulated screening provider, and a Swiss legal opinion confirming the corporate ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious pattern of tournament winnings and player prize payouts suggesting fungible unidentified funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-to-end player KYC/KYB policy, tournament rulebook and prize-fund custody rules, platform logic or smart-contract audit, daily transaction-reconciliation schema covering SWIFT, card acquiring, and API rails, withdrawal-velocity monitoring, and a compliance officer certification that the prize-pool settlements are attributable to identifiable players and verifiable competition results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border card settlements via Stripe and PayPal triggering merchant-risk or gambling-like indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial-model definition as software publishing, competitive matchmaking, and tournament management under ISIC 5820 and NAICS 711219, explicit exclusion of betting, gambling, and parimutuel activities, platform terms and conditions, absence of a statutory gambling license requirement, PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance attestation, fraud-prevention policy, and daily settlement caps designed to reduce layering risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Seed capital injection derived from cryptocurrency or tokenized wealth without a traceable fiat record
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level wallet history analyzed through a recognized chain-analysis tool, exchange statements and fiat off-ramp evidence from a FINMA-supervised Swiss bank or securities firm, written confirmation that the contributed assets are unencumbered, notarized certificate of source of wealth issued by a Swiss attorney, and the capital-payment confirmation from the receiving Swiss bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived lack of Swiss economic substance due to a substance-light structure with a non-resident board
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss registered-office agreement, active Commercial Register entry, annual financial statements and accounting records, board minutes showing strategic decisions, Swiss VAT registration (MWST), administrative or payroll service agreement with a Swiss provider, and a bank risk-assessment questionnaire evidencing genuine substance, local signatory authority, and the company's actual commercial activity in Switzerland.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing protocol: foreign shareholders must transmit equity contributions by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA shareholders) into the Swiss operational or capital account, denominated in CHF, EUR, or USD. The payment instructions should include the ISO 20022 purpose code CAPC (Capital Payment) and remittance text identifying the contribution as 'Einlage zur Erhöhung des Aktienkapitals der CH_AG'. The receiving Swiss bank applies AMLA-mandated payer screening and source-of-funds verification before the funds are released from any capital-blocking confirmation. For incorporation and capital increases, the Swiss Commercial Register requires a notarized bank confirmation (Bankbestätigung) that the minimum statutory capital is paid up and at the free disposal of the board. No Swiss National Bank approval or foreign-exchange permit is required for any amount, but amounts above CHF 10,000 will require documentary source-of-funds evidence. Crypto-asset contributions should be converted to fiat through a FINMA-supervised exchange before routing to the Swiss account; direct token transfers into a corporate bank account are operationally disfavored and may trigger extended due diligence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) domestic and cross-border euro payments through SIC, euroSIC, and Swiss Instant Payments (ISO 20022 credit transfers) for recurring prize payouts, supplier disbursements, and intra-group treasury flows; (ii) cross-border commercial settlements through SWIFT MT103 with gpi tracking, referencing suitable purpose codes such as TRAD, ROYA, or RENT and supported by invoices, tournament-results documentation, or licensing agreements; (iii) commercial and standby letters of credit issued through SWIFT MT700/MT799 for large media-rights acquisitions, broadcasting underwriting, and strategic tournament infrastructure contracts; and (iv) card and API acquiring rails, including Stripe and PayPal, which settle through European banking partners into the Swiss treasury account via SEPA or SWIFT. As the entity is a software publisher and esports platform rather than a physical-goods trader, transport documents are not mandatory, but the treasury must maintain a trade-settlement calendar and reconcile every outbound payment to an identified tournament, contract, licensing fee, or operating expense.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards between CHF and EUR, USD, or CNY with SNB-regulated Swiss or EU banking counterparties
FX swaps and rolling swap structures for managing tournament collections and payout currencies across settlement cycles
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) under an ISDA agreement for long-term financing or material foreign-currency capital structures

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for illiquid or non-convertible tournament-payout currencies where physical deliverability is unavailable; Swiss law does not prohibit NDFs, but CHF itself is fully convertible and deeply liquid, making CHF NDFs unnecessary
Vanilla foreign-currency options (puts and calls) to hedge uncertain timing and amount of prize-pool and sponsorship FX exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung) prepared, reviewed by the board, and presented for approval at the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders acting in the ordinary general meeting; no external filing with the commercial register unless a statutory publication obligation applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the balance-sheet date; the ordinary general meeting must be held within six months of the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No government late fee; non-compliance exposes directors to civil liability for damages, creditor enforcement, and criminal liability for false financial statements. Persistent failure may support a court-ordered liquidation petition.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory audit report (ordinary or limited audit) as required by the audit regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Statutory auditor (Revisionsstelle) reporting to the shareholders at the Annual General Meeting; retained by the company, not filed with the commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit report must be rendered in time for the Annual General Meeting, normally within six months of the balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or obtain the required audit can render the AGM resolution on the annual accounts ineffective, trigger court-ordered audit, and create director liability. No administrative strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal, cantonal, and communal corporate income tax return, including capital tax data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration as the single filing point for cantonal, communal, and federal direct taxes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year accounts, generally by 30 June of the following year, subject to cantonal filing calendars and extension requests
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger administrative fines up to approximately CHF 10,000, default interest, estimated tax assessments, and enforcement proceedings. Directors can become personally liable for taxes if the company is in arrears through their fault.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss Value Added Tax return (MWST-Abrechnung) for the applicable tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each quarter, six-month period, or fiscal year as approved by the VAT administration; annual VAT filing is available to qualifying small taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% per annum, administrative fines, penalty proceedings for late or incorrect returns, and criminal prosecution for deliberate VAT evasion. Tax debt is enforceable through debt collection measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage statement and social security settlement (AHV/IV/EO/ALV) for the esports platform's employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal compensation office / employer contribution clearing house (Ausgleichskasse)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage declaration and settlement generally due by 31 January of the year following the reporting calendar year; contributions are pre-paid on the statutory billing cycle during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest, enforced collection through debt enforcement proceedings, potential personal liability of directors for unpaid employer contributions, and administrative penalties for non-disclosure. No annual strike-off is triggered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-driven updates to the commercial register (registered office, directors, share capital, articles of association, or statutory facts)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) and publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not an annual date; filing must occur within the statutory notification window after the event giving rise to the registration obligation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file required changes triggers formal directions, administrative fines, and possible ex officio correction proceedings. Directors remain liable for inaccurate records. Administrative dissolution is reserved for exceptional cases such as loss of a lawful seat or bankruptcy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and maintenance of the shareholder register and beneficial ownership register, including share transfer entries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors and corporate records; no separate annual public filing to the commercial register is required under current federal law
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous duty; each share transfer and every known change of beneficial ownership must be recorded without undue delay, with an annual internal confirmation prepared for the board and, if applicable, the statutory auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective registers can invalidate exercise of membership rights, expose directors to liability for damages, and attract administrative penalties under anti-money-laundering and company law. Authorities may inspect records during official procedures; no annual strike-off mechanism applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss withholding tax declaration and payment for reportable income distributions (dividends, interest, royalties) if any are made
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Reporting and payment ordinarily due within 30 days after the end of the quarter in which the taxable payment obligation arose
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest and statutory penalties; the tax authority may enforce collection against the debtor company and pursue responsible officers. For a non-distributing startup, no return is required for the year.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit is compulsory if the company exceeds two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: CHF 20 million balance-sheet total, CHF 40 million annual turnover, or an average of 250 full-time employees. A limited audit is mandatory when the company has more than 10 full-time employees and is not subject to the ordinary audit. A full audit opt-out is available only for small companies with 10 or fewer full-time employees when all shareholders consent. Shareholders controlling 10% of the share capital may also require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting provisions (OR 957–965) for statutory accounts; Swiss GAAP FER for larger, listed, or regulated entities; IFRS is permitted for consolidated and certain listed reporting. No U.S. GAAP is applied for Swiss statutory purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss federal law does not currently impose an annual beneficial-ownership filing to a central public register for an ordinary Aktiengesellschaft. The company is required to maintain and continuously update an internal register of beneficial owners, identify the beneficial owner on each relevant share transfer, and provide the register for inspection by authorities and financial intermediaries in the context of AML/KYC reviews. For an esports community platform operating payment rails, the financial intermediary KYC confirmation is refreshed at least annually or upon a material change; the board should record an annual internal confirmation that the beneficial-ownership data remains accurate.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200–5,000 per year for Swiss registered office facilities, corporate agent, and administrative mail and compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–18,000 per year for an independent statutory audit, depending on entity size, transaction volume, and the audit form required (limited audit, ordinary audit, or opt-out documentation)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax on taxable net profit (statutory rate on profit after tax; equivalent to approximately 11.9% on pre-tax profit), plus cantonal/municipal net profit tax of approximately 4.5% to 17.5% depending on canton; in Zug the combined ordinary effective rate is approximately 14.6%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory amnesty-style tax holidays exist; Switzerland applies preferential structural deductions under the 2020 tax reform: cantonal patent box relief up to 90% of qualifying IP royalty income, incremental R&D super-deduction (up to 150% of qualifying R&D expenditures), optional notional interest deduction on excess equity (canton-level), federal participation relief (95% exemption for dividends and capital gains on qualifying participations of at least 10% or CHF 1,000,000 fair market value), and reduced capital tax rates in Zug; esports platform ordinary operating expenses including prize pools, tournament prize payouts, Stripe/PayPal settlement fees, bandwidth, licensing and player-acquisition costs are deductible as business expenses

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss corporate income tax return 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen' (Direct Federal Tax Declaration and combined Cantonal/Municipal Tax Declaration) filed electronically via the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for the direct federal tax and via the Cantonal Tax Administration portal (e.g., ePortal Steuerverwaltung Zug) for the cantonal/municipal taxes; the Aktiengesellschaft is assessed on net profit and paid-in capital
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the tax year coincides with the fiscal year; the AG makes quarterly provisional tax payments based on the latest final assessment and submits a single comprehensive annual return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline is generally six months after the fiscal year-end in accordance with Article 125 DBG for federal purposes and parallel cantonal rules; the competent tax administration routinely grants extensions up to nine months after year-end where the return is prepared and signed by a licensed Swiss fiduciary or certified public accountant, without penalty

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Main sheet — Net profit (Reingewinn / résultat net) line
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit as shown in the audited statutory financial statements after depreciation, valuation adjustments, provisions and generally accepted accounting practice (Swiss GAAP FER / IFRS) reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned AG files the full Swiss annual return identically to domestic entities; no consolidation pack is required unless the group's consolidated revenue exceeds the CHF 900,000,000 country-by-country reporting threshold; attach the statutory balance sheet and profit-and-loss statement with notes on shareholder advances

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross domestic and foreign dividend income from qualifying participations (at least 10% of nominal capital or CHF 1,000,000 fair market value); the AG claims the 95% participation deduction reducing effective federal and cantonal tax on that income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign dividend income gross before participation relief; attach ownership certificate, acquisition date evidence, and proof that the subsidiary is comparable to a Swiss company; relief will not apply to portfolio holdings below the statutory thresholds; dividend distributions sourced by the Swiss AG to its foreign parent are separate and subject to the 35% Swiss withholding tax regime

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible prior-year tax losses remaining within the seven consecutive-year carryforward period, assessed chronologically against the earliest assessable year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a loss inventory table reconciling each year's assessed loss to the current computation; Swiss law does not forfeit loss carryforwards upon a change of control, provided the AG continues its identical economic activity and no share-deal transaction constitutes an abusive loss trafficking arrangement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Withholding tax and profit repatriation annexes (Form 140 / Affidavit statements)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of all distributions, prizes, bond interest and finance payments made to shareholders and non-residents during the tax year, including the statutory 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividends and certain interest; royalties paid to non-residents are declared but bear 0% statutory withholding tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not remit dividends to the foreign parent until either a reduced-rate-at-source approval via Form 82 or an ex-post refund procedure via Form 85 is obtained from the ESTV; attach the foreign parent's tax residency certificate (TRC), beneficial ownership declaration and substance questionnaire

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Transfer pricing schedules and related-party disclosures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border trans actions with controlled affiliates: esports tournament platform license fees, matchmaking software royalties, management fees, administrative service reimbursements, and infrastructure costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Swiss tax law requires arm's-length bilateral positioning in accordance with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines upon audit; prepare and retain a local file/master file contemporary benchmark; groups exceeding CHF 900,000,000 consolidated revenue must file a Swiss country-by-country report in alignment with the ultimate parent's filing

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers procedural fines under Article 174 DBG up to CHF 30,000 for federal tax and equivalent cantonal procedural penalties up to approximately CHF 10,000; negligent under-assessment is fined under Article 175 DBG up to the amount of tax evaded with a maximum of CHF 10,000, while intentional tax fraud under Article 186 DBG attracts a fine up to three times the evaded federal tax and imprisonment up to three years; unpaid assessed tax accrues default interest at 4% to 5% per annum; directors who knowingly cause non-filing are jointly and severally liable under Articles 754 and 755 CO and may face travel bans and criminal extradition measures

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss withholding tax return (Verrechnungssteuer) — Form 140 (tax declaration for dividends, interest, lottery and prize payments) filed with the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) via the ISiTe electronic portal; quarterly provisional withholding tax remittances are made separately
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual declaration plus quarterly remittance of the 35% withholding tax within 30 days after each quarter-end, with final annual settlement on the statutory date
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The quantified annual declaration is due by 31 December of the following year for the previous calendar year; quarterly WHT payments must be remitted within 30 days after the end of each quarter; late remittance accrues WHT arrears interest of 5% per annum under Article 12 VStG

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Itemized list of each shareholder, gross dividend distributed, applicable withholding tax rate, and amount of 35% WHT withheld
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate whether a Form 82 reduced-rate approval was granted for each non-resident recipient and confirm beneficial ownership as at the distribution date; retaining the approved Form 82 in the corporate register avoids penalty recharacterization

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Prize pool and platform settlement classification (Stripe/PayPal payment flows)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line item distinguishing true tournament prize-pool pass-through disbursements from the platform's own commission revenue and from financing charges, to prevent accidental WHT characterization
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prize payments to resident and non-resident players in skill-based tournaments are ordinary business expenses without WHT; any technology service fee or license fee paid to a controlled foreign partner is reported as a royalty at 0% Swiss statutory WHT but may be recharacterized as constructive dividend under anti-abuse rules if lacking economic substance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under Article 67 VStG, intentional evasion of withholding tax is punished with a penalty up to ten times the evaded tax plus 5% arrears interest; failure to file or materially incomplete declarations under Article 66 VStG attract a fine up to CHF 15,000; the AG is liable for the unpaid WHT as a separate public-law debt with direct recourse against the board of directors personally for negligence or intent

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% gross Swiss withholding tax on dividends distributed by the Aktiengesellschaft under Article 4 VStG; non-residents may obtain treaty relief typically to 15% portfolio rate, 5% substantial participation rate (at least 10% holding), or 0% under aligned parent-subsidiary treaty provisions, subject to the beneficial ownership condition and satisfaction of economic substance requirements
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Two administrative tracks: (i) reduced-rate at source is obtained by filing Form 82 with the ESTV before distribution, accompanied by the foreign parent's tax residency certificate (TRC), proof of qualifying participation held for at least one year, and a Swiss formalized beneficial-ownership declaration; (ii) ex-post refund is claimed via Form 85 submitted within three years of the dividend payment date with the same documentation package; the ESTV verifies the recipient is not a mere pass-through shell and will deny relief under Article 21a VStG, Swiss GAAR (Article 56 DBG), and the Multilateral Convention principal purpose test; Form 140 annual declaration must reference every approved Form 82 position
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss statutory royalty withholding tax is 0% — no source tax applies to IP license or software royalty payments made by the Swiss esports platform to non-residents; statutory 35% withholding tax applies to paid interest on bonds and money-market paper issued by the AG, while ordinary bank interest and commercial trade interest are exempt; under Swiss double tax treaties, interest is reduced to 0%, 5% or 10% depending on the counterparty treaty, and royalties are typically reduced to 0% or 5%, with software fees analyzed under OECD royalty definitions; the platform must document all related-party debt and IP licensing on arm's-length terms to avoid reclassification as constructive dividend income

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Switzerland imposes no statutory monetary threshold that mandates the automatic filing of a Local File or Master File; however, documentation obligations arise on request during assessment or audit under Articles 58 and 175 DBG and Article 96 VStG, and the ESTV expects contemporaneous OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation whenever controlled transactions exist; the mandatory country-by-country reporting threshold is CHF 900,000,000 consolidated group revenue per Article 129a DBG, filed by the ultimate parent and exchanged automatically; taxpayers below that threshold are still required to retain sufficient arm's-length benchmarking documentation to substantiate all intercompany pricing on examination
approved_arm_length_methodologies: TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) — the Swiss default methodology for routine esports platform services
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has not enacted the BRC/UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; instead, substance is enforced through (1) Swiss GAAR under Article 56 DBG which disregards constructions lacking genuine economic purpose, (2) Article 21a VStG anti-abuse rules denying withholding tax and treaty relief to shell and letter-box companies, (3) the principal purpose test of the Multilateral Instrument, and (4) specific substance requirements for administrative, holding and domiciliary companies under ESTV circular practice; the Zug AG must maintain its registered seat, local statutory books, an operating bank account, locally resident directors with real decision-making authority, and adequate personnel and premises for the esports tournament platform activity to preserve the beneficial effective tax rate and to guarantee treaty access and dividend WHT reduction

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Tax Fraud — intentional false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting tournament commission income settled through Stripe/PayPal rails, maintaining undisclosed e-wallets, falsifying prize payout documentation to inflate deductions, issuing fake vendor invoices, or omitting related-party transactions from the annual return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal judicial tax fraud under Article 186 DBG: fine up to three times the evaded federal tax plus principal tax due with 4% to 5% default interest, and imprisonment up to three years; cantonal fraud penalties replicate at 100% to 300% of evaded tax; the assessment limitation period extends to ten years for fraudulent concealment and unpaid tax claims remain enforceable against the AG's assets for fifteen years; no amnesty applies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is authorized under Article 754 CO where directors intentionally or negligently cause tax damage; civil restitution claims are pursued jointly and severally against all board members; criminal convictions under Article 186 DBG expose resident and non-resident directors to arrest warrants, travel bans, and extradition under Switzerland's mutual legal assistance framework; the cantonal tax collection office may order an exit block against directors who fail to secure unpaid assessed corporate tax

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Default and Undeclared Dividend Remittances
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or constructive benefits to a foreign parent without withholding the statutory 35%, distributing before obtaining Form 82 approval or awaiting Form 85 refund, using circular loans, back-to-back financing, or artificial prize-pool transfers to disguise profit distributions and circumvent WHT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 67 VStG penalty of up to ten times the unpaid withholding tax plus 5% arrears interest from the due date; the AG's claim to repayment rights is forfeited and the unpaid WHT becomes a secured federal claim enforceable by asset attachment; directors who signed the distribution minutes are subject to direct liability notices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the designated tax representative are personally liable under Articles 12 and 67 VStG even where the AG is insolvent; the ESTV routinely issues personal payment orders and opens criminal proceedings against at least one locally resident director; personal bank accounts and real property of directors are seizable and, in aggravated cases, imprisonment up to three years is imposed for intentional non-collection of withholding tax

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Abuse and Artificial Profit Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging inflated royalties, license fees, management fees or administrative markups to the foreign parent to reduce Swiss taxable profit; failing to pay arm's-length compensation to the Swiss platform for tournament hosting services; misclassifying eSports player data or matchmaking technology as owned by the parent without substance; engaging in treaty-shopping through a parent located in a low-tax jurisdiction without economic activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary reassessment under Article 58 DBG within the seven-to-ten-year reassessment window: TP adjustment increases taxable profit, attracts constructive dividend taxation at the 35% WHT level and triggers the 8.5% federal plus Zug cantonal taxes at the denied rates; negligence surcharge up to CHF 10,000 under Article 175 DBG; fraud enhancements apply up to three times the reassessed tax; the MLI principal purpose test allows treaty benefits denial with retroactive effect
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and CFOs are personally liable under Article 754 CO for TP adjustment damages, including penalties and arrears interest; foreign parent directors are reachable through administrative assistance and mutual legal assistance treaties; Switzerland permits civil seizure of directors' personal assets where the AG is structured as a profit-shifting conduit; criminal conviction as accomplices under Article 186 DBG carries imprisonment up to three years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the esports community platform without Swiss Anti-Money-Laundering Act (AMLA) due diligence on tournament winners, prize payouts and aggregated Stripe/PayPal settlement flows; failing to establish and document beneficial ownership; implementing nominee shareholders or nominee directors without local substance; maintaining the AG as an invoice shell for foreign principals
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 11 AMLA: imprisonment up to three years and a fine up to CHF 500,000 for intentional violation of due diligence, reporting, and record-keeping duties; FINMA notices the Federal Tax Administration and treats the AG as non-substantive, triggering withdrawal of payment processor accounts and bank facilities; the AG may be struck from the commercial register following insolvency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who control payment settlement or sign platform agreements bear criminal liability independently of the corporate entity; the five-year AMLA prescription does not shield board members; Swiss financial institutions blacklist involved directors, and compliance officers may be personally banned from holding regulated banking roles; civil restitution to defrauded stakeholders and tax authorities is enforced against directors' personal estates

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Regulatory Contamination from Gambling and Chance-Based Tournament Mechanics
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Offering real-money tournament entry fees combined with chance-based prize distributions or randomized matchmaking rewards to Swiss residents without the required authorization under the Swiss Federal Act on Money Games (Geldspielgesetz); failing to distinguish skill-based eSports competition from prohibited casino-type gaming; overpaying prize disbursements through unlicensed small-gaming schemes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to CHF 500,000, disgorgement of gaming revenue, and closure orders from the Cantonal Lottery and Betting Commission; tax consequences include disallowance of prize expense deductions, full taxation of undeclared prize pools, revocation of the reduced Zug cantonal rate for the relevant assessment period, and retroactive re-assessment with 5% interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tournament organizers face criminal responsibility under the Money Games Act, with imprisonment up to three years for organized unlicensed gaming; repeated violations are treated as commercial fraud, enabling civil claims by participant losers against directors' personal assets; a criminal conviction additionally voids directors' suitability under Swiss corporate law and precludes the AG from obtaining future cantonal licensing
